name: Notte

modes.label: Browser session
modes.note: Runtime free; proxy, LLM, account and functions can bill. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: Browser function
modes.note: Serverless function runtime separate from free browser session; billed per billing policy. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: $10 once; 5 vaults/personas; features included per current pricing.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom limits, BYOC/on-prem, SSO, HIPAA, SLA.

features.ip_note: Residential proxies $10/GB, billed only when proxies are enabled, BUT managed residential proxies are ON by default (API/SDK `proxies` default true; best-effort US exit). Every session bills $10/GB of its traffic unless the caller passes proxies=false or a BYO proxy. IP used with proxies off is undocumented. BYO HTTP/HTTPS proxy and Tailscale egress; BYO proxy listed on Startup/Enterprise only.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

docs.notte.cc/pricing and /rate-limits now 307-redirect to www.notte.cc/pricing (the authoritative source). Stale figures survive only in the docs llms-full.txt bundle (100 forever/100 monthly/500 monthly browser hours, Free concurrency 2, Developer 30 min, Startup 3 h, credit packs $100/$200/$500) and on the functions invocations page ('Free: 10 concurrent runs, Pro: 50 concurrent runs'). Ignore those; use the pricing page.
Free browser time is not free proxies/inference/serverless functions. No 4/8 resource guarantee and no general snapshots.
Included monthly fees are credits, not fee+full usage. Top-ups and signup $10 never expire; monthly balances do.
os set to linux (fix 2026-09-28): hosted cloud browser sessions run server-side; the guest OS is not published but they are not a macOS/Windows desktop.

Managed residential proxies are enabled by default on every session (proxies=true default) and bill $10/GB; pass proxies=false (or a BYO proxy on Startup+) to keep a session near $0. Default proxy exit is best-effort US.

Browser runtime was $0.05/hour until about 2026-09-01 (docs PR #923 'Browser usage is now $0/hour'); no end date is published for $0/hour, so price_expires stays null, but it is a recent cut worth re-checking.

open_source=true only in the loose sense: the nottelabs/notte repo is SSPL-1.0 (source-available, not OSI), and it is the agent/SDK framework, not the hosted browser platform (on-prem is Enterprise-only).

API request rate limit: documented via X-RateLimit-* headers with an example limit of 100 requests per window (window length not published); 429 on excess; higher limits via sales ('Contact us ... enterprise options'). Per-plan start/creation rate limits are not published.

Enterprise-only: multi-region (llms-full lists us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast), static IPs, browser pools (pre-warmed), on-prem/BYOC; advanced_stealth is approval-gated. Self-serve region is not published (features.regions left null).
Functions gained an 'extended' runtime (SDK v1.8.41, 2026-09-09) for longer cloud execution; the pricing page only lists one $0.05/hour function rate, so extended-runtime pricing is unpublished.

fleet.notes: Browser and agent/function concurrency published separately with same 5/25/100 ladder. 10 fits Developer, 50 Startup, 300/1,000 Enterprise. Credits and session-duration limits additionally apply.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: `True` - Save browser state to the profile when the session ends
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in browser-profile persistence (profile persist=True, or cookie_file) saves cookies/browser storage when the session ends and reloads it in the next session; treated as a persistent-profile (persistent_disk analogue), not a machine snapshot. No memory/tabs/process state; no general snapshots documented.

own_agent_api.quote: Stream agent logs in real-time via WebSocket:
own_agent_api.note: Notte's own browser agent only: POST /agents/start with a task (plus session, vault, persona, max_steps, response format), GET status with steps, WebSocket log streaming, stop, list agents, MP4 replay, export run as workflow code. No follow-up/continue endpoint documented. Claude Code/Claude Managed Agents etc. use Notte from outside via CLI/MCP.

harness_api.quote: Stream agent logs in real-time via WebSocket:
harness_api.note: Notte's own browser agent only: POST /agents/start with a task (plus session, vault, persona, max_steps, response format), GET status with steps, WebSocket log streaming, stop, list agents, MP4 replay, export run as workflow code. No follow-up/continue endpoint documented. Claude Code/Claude Managed Agents etc. use Notte from outside via CLI/MCP.

ingress_rules.quote: The returned URL is signed with a short-lived JWT scoped to that session
ingress_rules.note: No user-exposed ports; session API/CDP needs the API key and the live-view/embed URL is a short-lived session-scoped JWT link. No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.note: Hosted cloud browser (card isolation: container) reachable only through API/CDP; no shell/root, so no nftables/iptables. Serverless Functions run user Python but no root/network-namespace details are documented.

secret_proxy.quote: The significant security benefit of this approach is that the LLM never actually sees the actual credentials.
secret_proxy.note: Not an outbound HTTP credential proxy. Vaults substitute real credentials for dummy values in the agent's fill actions (passwords, cards, MFA/TOTP), so the LLM never sees them, but the value is typed into the browser. Workspace /secrets store: 'llm_provider' keys used server-side by agents (BYOK) and 'function_env' values injected into function runs as env. The Claude Managed Agents guide's placeholder substitution is Anthropic's vault, not Notte's.

isolation.quote: os set to linux; hosted cloud browser sessions run server-side, guest OS not published
isolation.note: Card-level field carried over: hosted managed browser/Functions platform, no VM/microVM details published; treated as shared-kernel container isolation, medium confidence.

image_oci.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No custom Docker/OCI image support documented for sessions or Functions; Functions are Python scripts (run() entrypoint) deployed as source code, not container images.

docker_inside.quote: Functions are Python scripts with a `run()` function that serves as the entry point.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No Docker/container runtime documented inside browser sessions or the Functions Python runtime.

nested_virt.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No shell/root access or /dev/kvm is documented; product is a managed browser/Python-function API, not a general VM.

desktop.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Notte exposes a browser (live-view iframe/CDP), not a general graphical desktop with VNC/RDP for a full OS.

ssh.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No SSH/shell access to the underlying browser or Function machine is documented; access is only via the HTTP/SDK/CDP/MCP API.

snapshot.quote: A profile is a saved snapshot of a browser's user data directory. By default, each Notte session uses a fresh browser state to ensure isolation.
snapshot.note: Only opt-in browser-profile persistence (cookies/local storage of the user-data dir) exists, not a general machine disk or memory snapshot with running processes restored. No documented full-machine snapshot/restore feature for sessions or Functions.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A profile is a saved snapshot of a browser's user data directory.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Profile save happens on session end/via API for cookies/storage, not an on-demand full machine checkpoint. No general snapshot/checkpoint API documented.

fork.quote: Fork a shared function into your own private function
fork.note: Only Notte Functions (Python code/config) can be forked (copy code from marketplace/teammate into your own account); this is a code copy, not cloning a running browser session/machine. No session/machine fork documented.

fork_running.quote: Fork a shared function into your own private function
fork_running.note: not offered: Function fork copies code (function not running at fork time); no running-session/machine clone-without-stopping capability documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Fork a shared function into your own private function
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: fork only copies Function source code; no memory/process state is included since there is no running-machine fork feature at all.

pause_resume.quote: Idle timeout in minutes. Session closes after this period of inactivity (resets on each operation).
pause_resume.note: Idle sessions are closed (terminated) after the idle timeout, not paused for later resume; no pause/resume-with-reduced-billing API is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Idle timeout in minutes. Session closes after this period of inactivity (resets on each operation).
wake_on_request.note: Sessions close on idle timeout rather than sleep; a new request starts a new session rather than waking a suspended one. No auto-wake-on-request feature documented.

persistent_disk.quote: By default, each Notte session uses a fresh browser state to ensure isolation.
persistent_disk.note: Sessions are ephemeral by default; only opt-in browser-profile (cookies/storage) persists across sessions, which is a narrow persisted-profile feature, not a general persistent filesystem/disk surviving stop/start.

volume_attach.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No attachable persistent volume feature is documented; per-session file storage (upload/download session files) is session-scoped, not an attachable volume.

volume_shared.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No shared-volume-across-machines feature is documented.

live_resize.quote: Runtime free; proxy, LLM, account and functions can bill.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No published vCPU/RAM sizing exists for browser sessions to begin with (sizes card leaves vcpu/ram null), so there is no documented live-resize-of-a-running-machine capability.

agent_harnesses.quote: This works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP-compatible assistants.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Notte connects to external coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) as an MCP tool client from the user's own machine; it does not preinstall or offer coding-agent harnesses running inside its own sandboxes.

mcp_server.quote: Give any MCP client access to Notte.
mcp_server.note: First-party MCP server at https://api.notte.cc/mcp/ (streamable HTTP, bearer auth) exposing sessions, browser agents, scraping, functions, vaults and personas as MCP tools.

lang_python.quote: Functions are Python scripts with a `run()` function that serves as the entry point.
lang_python.note: Serverless Functions execute user-authored Python code server-side; Python SDK (notte_sdk) is also first-party.

lang_node.quote: Functions are Python scripts with a `run()` function that serves as the entry point.
lang_node.note: Notte Functions only execute Python; the Node/TypeScript SDK (notte-sdk) is a client for calling the API from Node, not a runtime that executes JS/TS code inside the sandbox.

public_ipv4.quote: Static IPs provide dedicated, unchanging IP addresses for your browser sessions... available exclusively for enterprise customers.
public_ipv4.note: not offered on self-serve: outside default product scope. Documented IP features are outbound-only (residential proxy egress IP, enterprise static egress IP); no inbound public IPv4 per machine is offered since the product is not general inbound compute.

inbound_https.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only the session live-view/embed URL (short-lived JWT-scoped) is exposed inbound; there is no general capability to expose arbitrary ports on the machine over HTTPS.

egress_allowlist.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No documented provider-side outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode; egress is a browsing/proxy configuration (residential proxy on/off, BYO proxy, Tailscale egress), not a security-group-style allowlist.

egress_http_rules.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts, vaults, personas, mailboxes.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented.

gpu.quote: Notte gives your agent a browser -- sessions, a serverless Function runtime for Python scripts.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No GPU machine option is published for a browser-automation/Python-function API.

windows.quote: hosted cloud browser sessions run server-side; the guest OS is not published but they are not a macOS/Windows desktop
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Confirmed by card research: guest OS is not a selectable Windows desktop.

macos.quote: hosted cloud browser sessions run server-side; the guest OS is not published but they are not a macOS/Windows desktop
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Confirmed by card research: guest OS is not a selectable macOS desktop.

eu_data_residency.quote: Data residency - Keep data processing within specific regions ... Multi-Region Support is available exclusively for enterprise customers.
eu_data_residency.note: Multi-region support (llms-full.txt lists us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) is documented as an Enterprise-only, sales-gated feature enabling EU-region processing; not available self-serve on Free/Developer/Startup.

usage_api.quote: GET /usage returns account-level usage with browser_usage_cost, proxy_usage_cost, llm_usage_cost, function_usage_cost, total_cost, session_count, and function_count; no per-session breakdown endpoint documented. /usage/logs provides operational logs only (created_at, duration_ms, endpoint), not bill
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; Notte's /usage endpoint aggregates costs and session/function counts at the account level. The /usage/logs endpoint provides operational metrics (duration, endpoint) but not cost breakdown per individual session or sandbox. No documented endpoint returns billable usage by session ID, tag, project, or label.

locations_quote: Multi-Region Support is available exclusively for enterprise customers. Contact andrea@notte.cc to learn more about enterprise plans and regional deployment options.
